The user asks about PostgreSQL version 16 support under upstream community policy (not vendor extended support), as of 2026-10-07. Need to determine: is major version 16 supported at cutoff? Scheduled final release date? How long major versions are supported and when the clock begins? Does installing a newer 16.x minor restart the clock?

Need to use websearch and webfetch. Let's search.

Key sources: PostgreSQL versioning policy page (https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/), PostgreSQL roadmap (https://www.postgresql.org/developer/roadmap/), maybe release notes. Upstream policy: each major release supported 5 years from initial release. PostgreSQL 16 released September 14, 2023. So EOL November 2028 (typically the second Thursday of November? Actually final release usually in November of the year 5 years after). Let me verify.

PostgreSQL 16 initial release: 2023-09-14. Supported for 5 years, until November 2028 (final release Nov 2028). The versioning policy says: "PostgreSQL major versions are supported for five years from the date of their initial release." Minor releases do not extend support: "the minor releases do not have separate support timelines; upgrading to a newer minor does not extend the support period for the major version."

As of 2026-10-07, PostgreSQL 16 is supported (within 5 years of Sep 2023, until Nov 2028). Scheduled final release date: November 9, 2028? Need source. The roadmap page lists upcoming releases; maybe final release date for 16 is November 2028. Let me check.

Let's do searches.
